key_insight: All 54 evaluated quaternary mixed-metal chalcohalides are thermodynamically unstable, but many sit close enough to the convex hull to remain plausible synthesis targets.
engineering_relevance: For solution-processing workflows, convex-hull proximity and likely competing phases can be used to prioritize which mixed-anion semiconductors are worth attempting first.
method: DFT stability calculations for 54 M(II)2M(III)Ch2X3 compounds
Cross-referenced predictions with the Alexandria Materials Database
Compared predicted decomposition pathways against experimental solution-processing results
evidence_signal: The study combines density functional theory with database screening and experimental validation on six Sn-based compounds, including first synthesis of Sn2InS2Br3 in a multiphase film.
watch_item: Computational uncertainty near the hull means apparent accessibility may not translate into clean phase-pure synthesis, especially when multiple competing phases are present.
paper_title: How Thermodynamically Accessible are Quaternary Mixed-Metal Chalcohalides?
